Ravi (sales): Urgent POC issue — GlobalRetail is seeing truncation / context cutoff when they send product catalogs as a single massive `messages` entry (~1.9MB raw JSON). Demo in 6 hours. Any quick wins?

Ana (solutions): Are they using the chat endpoint with messages array? We should confirm whether they embed full product JSON in `content` or attach it in `meta`.

Ravi (sales): They embed it directly in content. Example snippet from their client: `{"role":"user","content": "<<huge JSON catalog here>>"}`. They claim they need the full catalog to be included for zero-shot QA.

Diego (eng): Two things: (1) our frontend LB + API gateway enforce ~2MB JSON body limit on hosted; (2) model context max tokens also matter — even if we accept the payload, the tokenizer might truncate. What does their catalog expand to in tokens?

Priya (eng-ml): Quick estimate: 1.9MB UTF-8 JSON ~ ~450k characters ~ ~225k tokens (varies). Our models typically cap at 32k tokens for inference. So truncation will happen irrespective of ingress limits. Need to recommend chunking or retrieval-augmented approaches.

Ravi (sales): Customer insists they need the whole catalog in context for the demo to show exact-match QA. Any demo-friendly trick?

Ana (solutions): Workarounds: 1) For demo, host a temporary index: we ingest the catalog into a lightweight vector DB and use a retrieval step to pull top-k relevant docs. 2) If they truly need the whole JSON verbatim, compress + base64 + gzip might fit under the LB limit but will still hit token limits at model side. 3) Use a smaller schema: only include item identifiers and indexes in context and fetch metadata on demand.

Diego (eng): For immediate demo: spin up an ephemeral retrieval proxy that accepts their giant JSON POST, stores it in S3, runs a quick embedding pass (we can sample or chunk) and returns an API that the front-end calls instead of embedding. That avoids changing their client code beyond endpoint swap.

Priya (eng-ml): For demo, we can also run an on-the-fly summarization: chunk the catalog into 5-10K token pieces, summarize each, and pass concatenated summaries as context. That keeps token count low and preserves salient info. Explain to the customer that it's an approximation.

Ravi (sales): Which option is fastest to implement by the demo?

Ana (solutions): Quickest: proxy + S3 + presigned URL + small retrieval. Takes ~1-2 hours with our tooling. Summarization pipeline might take longer but could be scripted from our eval harness in ~3 hours. Gzip trick is risky and won't solve token limits.

Diego (eng): I'll stand up the proxy and pre-sign flow. Priya, can you give a summarization script snippet?

Priya (eng-ml): Pseudocode for chunk+summarize:

```
chunks = chunk_text(catalog_json, max_chars=80000)
summaries = [model.summarize(c) for c in chunks]
context = '\n'.join(summaries)
response = model.chat(prompt + context)
```

Mention that chunk boundaries should preserve JSON object boundaries to avoid corrupting entries.

charlie-bot: Created TASK-5587: ephemeral-proxy-for-poc (owner: diego).

Ravi (sales): Solid. Please keep me posted. I'll tell GlobalRetail we have a fallback retrieval demo to show later today. Also confirm pricing note? If we do embeddings + retrieval, how will billing look?

Ana (solutions): Embeddings are billed per embedding unit + retrieval queries per call. For demo estimates: embedding the catalog once is one-time cost. Serving retrievals incur per-request tokens for prompt + returned snippets. I'll draft a short cost estimate and DM you.

Diego (eng): Done setting up the proxy; endpoint: https://poc-proxy.internal/ingest — it returns `catalog_id`. Frontend can then call `/qa?catalog_id=...&query=...`.

Ravi (sales): Thanks team. I'll use the proxy approach for the demo and follow up on a permanent architecture recommendation.

Priya (eng-ml): Long term: we should add a Support doc titled "Handling large contexts: retrieval & chunking patterns" and add automated guidance/error messages when payloads exceed token or ingress limits.

Ravi (sales): +1. Please ping when doc is up so I can attach to the post-demo notes.
